messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Smart-routing fallback rate > 20% for region-us-west; automated fallback to model-variant `m-llama-v2-quant` triggered repeatedly. Correlation: recent manual force-routing changes noted. Please acknowledge and investigate.
PagerDuty: Page sent to @Sasha (oncall). Escalation policy: 5m
Sasha: ack — pulling router logs and fallback traces now.
Mike: i'm seeing a stream of routing-change events from the control plane — looks like a manual force to `region-eu-1` earlier caused sticky sessions for some customers.
Priya: what do you mean by sticky? router state didn't expire?
Sasha: router entries were marked as pinned -> `force_region: eu-1` for several client routes. The policy engine still had a fallback rule that redirects to `m-llama-v2-quant` when eu-1 is chosen. Combined, that created a cascade: pinned region -> variant fallback -> saturation -> more pins.
Jordan: impact: 1.8k requests/min with >10% 5xx in the last 3m across two enterprise tenants. Latency  p50 -> 1.2s, p95 -> 4.8s for affected routes.
Lee: confirmed increased KV cache eviction on serving nodes in eu-1 after the pin; memory churn causing long scheduling pauses.
Priya: can we stop the pin quickly? who did the force?
Mike: timestamped audit: `sasha.ops` did a manual `force-region` command at 1977768200 to drain a degraded pool. It looks like the CLI flag used had no TTL, so it didn't unwind automatically.
Sasha: that was me — I forced eu-1 to move traffic off a failing host, but i didn't realize it would persist across policy reconciles. my bad.
Priya: ok stop — do NOT apply any more manual forces until we coordinate. We need a safe unwind plan.
Mike: quick mitigation proposal: 1) revert the manual force (unpin) 2) set a short-lived soft-pin with TTL 3) roll traffic to `m-llama-v2-small` for affected routes as a lower-cost-compatible variant 4) throttle burst QPS for enterprise tenants to avoid cascade.
Sasha: i'm going to revert the pin now. executing:
```
# remove forced region tag from router DB
redwood-routerctl unpin-route --route-id r-12345 --reason "revert emergency pin"
```
ops-bot: command received, initiating unpin workflow. Will emit status events here.
ops-bot: Unpin job started (job id j-98321). Watching reconciliation.
Priya: while unpin runs, please stage fallback variant to small, but do not change traffic weights until we confirm unpin succeeded.
Mike: preparing rollout: checkbox list -> `canary 5% -> monitor 2m -> ramp`
Jordan: customer comms: drafting note. Two affected customers (AcmeCorp, DataWave) are hitting tokenization failures when routed to quant variant; they should be notified if we expect >15m impact.
Sasha: unpin job returned: FAILED — reconciliation loop detected: control-plane still has an active policy that re-applies `force_region: eu-1` from policy id p-445. Looks like there is a higher-priority policy (legacy emergency) still active.
Priya: where did that policy come from?
Mike: that legacy policy is from a previous incident; it was marked "manual emergency" and never deactivated. It has a higher precedence than route-level unpin.
Lee: this is why we need a two-step: disable policy, then unpin.
Sasha: i'm disabling policy p-445 now via console.
Sasha: disabled policy p-445. running unpin again.
ops-bot: policy-disable event logged (audit id a-772), unpin job requeued.
ops-bot: Unpin job completed successfully. Router reconciliation shows no pinned entries for r-12345.
Mike: ok proceed with controlled variant swap to `m-llama-v2-small` at 5% canary now.
Priya: starting canary: route update posted to control plane.
Priya: monitoring canary metrics...
Jordan: canary telemetry: p50 120ms, p95 450ms, error-rate 0.4% — much better than quant variant.
Sasha: traffic shifted to small for 5% canary successfully.
Mike: ramp to 30% over next 4m if metrics hold. Also applying temporary per-tenant burst rate limit for AcmeCorp and DataWave to 200 QPS to protect backend.
Jordan: customer comms ready: "We've identified a routing policy conflict that kept traffic pinned to a stressed region and variant. We've reverted the emergency policy, unpinned routes, and are rolling traffic to a safer variant. Expect normal service within 15-30m. We will follow up with root cause analysis."
Priya: good. two operational followups: 1) add TTL to any future manual force commands (default 15m) 2) add a policy-dependency check in the unpin runbook so disabling a policy is required before unpin can succeed.
Sasha: agree. I'll own the runbook patch and the CLI default.
Mike: i'll open an incident postmortem and assign action items: runbook, CLI default TTL, and add an automated guard that prevents higher-priority active policies from reapplying pins without explicit approval.
Lee: note for infra: check EU-1 serving pool for memory fragmentation and KV cache compaction. schedule a maintenance window if needed.
ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> active-> monitoring. Next update in 15m or sooner if regression.
Sasha: oncall handoff to Mike in 30m. leaving notes in the incident doc. :thumbsup:
PagerDuty: Acknowledgement recorded. Incident page closed if no further alerts within 15m.
Jordan: thanks team. we'll collect logs and snapshots for RCA.
Mike: quick log snippet for RCA reference:
```
router.events: [
  {"ts":1977768200, "event":"force_region_set", "actor":"sasha.ops", "policy":null},
  {"ts":1977768300, "event":"policy_apply", "policy":"p-445", "note":"legacy emergency"},
  {"ts":1977770000, "event":"fallback_trigger", "variant":"m-llama-v2-quant"}
]
```
Sasha: i'll add my timeline. apologies for the operational fallout — learned to check policy precedence before forcing.
Priya: thanks for the quick handling. Postmortem owners: Mike (writeup), Sasha (runbook/CLI fix), Lee (infra check), Priya (policy cleanup).
ops-bot: Incident state -> resolved pending monitoring.
